tokens.STACK_SUMMARY: A multi-skill Agent Skills pack (kdcllc/skills) distributed through skills.sh, the Claude Code and Cursor plugin marketplaces, and `gh skill`. Every folder under `skills/<name>/` is a published skill (`SKILL.md` + `CHANGELOG.md`, optional `scripts/`, `references/`, `assets/`), versioned on its own via `metadata.version` and released as `<name>/vX.Y.Z` tags. The largest skill is `agent-kit` — the orchestration kit compiler: canonical Claude-format templates under `skills/agent-kit/templates/`, per-harness emitter caveats under `skills/agent-kit/emitters/`, deterministic emitter twins under `skills/agent-kit/bin/`, and a verified harness capability matrix under `skills/agent-kit/reference/`. Maintainer research lives in `docs/agent-kit/`. Executable code is bash + PowerShell twins (emitters, loop drivers, self-install, checks) plus per-skill helper scripts. There is no application runtime — verification is structural: `scripts/validate-skills.sh` (layout, frontmatter, versions, marketplaces, `scripts/checks/*.sh` guards) and the agent-kit suites under `tests/agent-kit/`.
tokens.EXECUTION_LAYERS: skills/<name>/ (published skills; agent-kit: templates/ → bin/ + emitters/ → reference/harness-matrix.md) → scripts/checks/ + tests/ → docs/ + root README.md / skills.sh.json / marketplace manifests
tokens.QA_SURFACES: - **Emitted install artifacts** — the output a /agent-kit run produces in a target project. Evidence: grep output proving zero unresolved tokens/bootstrap comments; frontmatter validation (every `name:` matches its folder/file); `bash -n` output for the emitted loop.sh; link-check output proving relative links in the emitted README/architecture doc resolve.

tokens.EVALUATOR_AUTO_FAIL_TRIGGERS:
- Unresolved '{{...}}' template token, or a leftover bootstrap comment (an HTML
  comment opening with the word BOOTSTRAP), in any emitted/instance file.
- A template token used anywhere under skills/agent-kit/templates/ that is not documented
  in the placeholder table of skills/agent-kit/SKILL.md.
- Frontmatter `name:` not matching its folder name (skills) or file name (agents).
- Hardcoded model IDs anywhere outside the model map (canonical:
  skills/agent-kit/templates/models.map.md; instance: {{IDE_DIR}}/skills/agent-kit-models.map.md).
- Instance- or session-specific content leaked INTO canonical templates — the
  canonical kit under skills/agent-kit/ must stay project-agnostic (product isolation).
- Template ↔ emitter drift — an emitter under skills/agent-kit/emitters/ referencing
  files, paths, or keys that no longer exist in templates/.

bootstrap.fallback-chains:
| Tier | Chain (first available wins) |
|------|------------------------------|
| `frontier` | `claude-opus-5-5` → `claude-sonnet-5-5` → (omit pin — harness default) |
| `light` | `claude-sonnet-5-5` → `claude-haiku-5-5` → (omit pin — harness default) |
| `fast` | `claude-haiku-5-5` → `claude-sonnet-5-5` → (omit pin — harness default) |

Cursor fallback (same policy, Cursor IDs): `claude-opus-5-5-high` → `composer-2.5-fast`
→ (omit pin); light: `composer-2.5-fast` → (omit pin). Cursor silently substitutes a
compatible model under team-admin/plan restrictions, or when the resolved ID is
unknown/stale (a rotated-out or misspelled model name) — evaluators must report which
model produced the verdict.
bootstrap.frontier-alt-family:
| Ladder step | Model pin |
|-------------|-----------|
| Diagnosis-driven implementation attempt (rung 4) | Claude Code `claude-opus-5-5` / Cursor `claude-opus-5-5-high` |
| Evaluator arbitration mode (rung 5) | Claude Code `claude-opus-5-5` / Cursor `claude-opus-5-5-high` — same-family arbiter (reduced independence) |
bootstrap.loop-fallback:
| Chain (first available wins) | Resolves |
|-------------------------------|----------|
| `claude-sonnet-5-5` → `claude-haiku-5-5` → (omit pin — harness default) | `claude-sonnet-5-5,claude-haiku-5-5` |

Light-tier by default — the loop's iterations are implementer/test-writer-shaped work,
same as the `light` row above. Ends with the same omit-the-pin rule as the tables
above: a trip past the last chain entry clears the model pin and the harness default
takes over (no hardcoded model IDs outside this file). The resolved chain is one
comma-separated string with no spaces around commas — neither driver twin trims chain
entries. Never use `best` or `fable` in the chain — emit rejects them (usage-credit billing).
bootstrap.models-map-caveats:
- **Claude Code env overrides**: `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` and
  `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` override frontmatter; org `availableModels` allowlists can
  cause pins to be ignored.
- **Claude Code is single-provider (Anthropic only)**: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` changes the
  endpoint, not the model family — a different-family arbiter is unreachable natively
  (see **Same-family arbiter** in this file).
- **Claude Code aliases resolve per provider**: an alias such as `opus` maps to a
  different model on Microsoft Foundry, Bedrock, or Google Cloud than on the Anthropic
  API — prefer full IDs. Minimum Claude Code versions for these pins: Opus 5.5 ≥
  v2.1.280, Sonnet 5.5 ≥ v2.1.284, Haiku 5.5 ≥ v2.1.293.
- **Claude Code usage-credit aliases**: headless loop runs must never resolve to
  `best`/`fable` (they bill usage credits without asking); emit rejects them in a loop
  chain.
- Model values: Claude aliases or full IDs are both valid; `inherit` is the frontmatter
  default if a tier is deliberately unpinned.
- **Cursor silent fallback**: under team-admin/plan restrictions, or when the resolved
  ID is unknown/stale (a rotated-out or misspelled model name), Cursor substitutes a
  compatible model without erroring — evaluators should state their expected model in
  their prompt and report which model produced the verdict.
- **Cursor Cloud Agents** are main→L1 only; the QA-gate flow still works, but
  nested L2 worker spawns from an L1 agent are not available in cloud.
bootstrap.models-map-effort:
Reasoning-effort pins: evaluators (`evaluator`, `qa-evaluator`) `high`,
`diagnostician` `xhigh`, `implementer`/`test-writer` `medium`, `terminal` `low` — Claude
Code `effort:` frontmatter. On Cursor, effort for the pinned Claude slugs is carried in
picker-verified suffix form (`claude-opus-5-5-high`, `claude-sonnet-5-5-xhigh`);
`composer-2.5-fast` is Composer's speed/price variant (Fast tier), not an effort suffix.
Bracket params appended to the model ID (`<model-id>[effort=high]`) are documented
frontmatter but were not verified on this account at emit time. Never quote the YAML
`model:` value — a quoted or unresolvable value silently falls back to the parent model.
bootstrap.models-map-fix-cycle:
| Fix cycle | Implementer model |
|-----------|-------------------|
| 1 | Claude Code `claude-sonnet-5-5` (normal) / Cursor `composer-2.5-fast` (normal) |
| 2 | Claude Code `claude-opus-5-5`; Cursor `claude-sonnet-5-5-xhigh` |
| 3 | Claude Code `claude-opus-5-5` with effort `xhigh`; Cursor `claude-opus-5-5-high` |

### Emitted install artifacts (the output of a /agent-kit run in a target project)

- Zero unresolved '{{...}}' template tokens and zero leftover bootstrap comments in
  every emitted file — demonstrated by grep output over the full emitted tree.
- Every emitted agent and skill file has valid frontmatter and its `name:` matches its
  folder name (skills) or file name (agents) — demonstrated by validation output.
- The emitted `_loop/loop.sh` passes `bash -n` and is executable.
- Relative links in the emitted README section and architecture doc
  (ORCHESTRATION.md instance) resolve to real files — demonstrated by link-check
  output.
- The emitted model map is the only place model IDs appear; agent frontmatter uses the
  tiers/aliases it defines.
- The manifest (`orchestration-kit.manifest.json`) lists every emitted file with a
  correct sha256.
